audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor is stale relative to the 2026 claim
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 filed net income was $579m versus $177m in FY2024, a $402m increase; OE and valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Replaces the latest-actual OE anchor and aligns the earnings numerator with the June 2026 bridge and shares
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2024, Net income attributable to HF Sinclair stockholders was $177 million compared to $1,590 million and $2,923 million for the years ended December 31, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated dating error: the supplied 2025 10-K contains a completed FY2025, yet the valuation anchors on FY2024. FY2025 and first-half 2026 results differ substantially from FY2024, but net income cannot substitute for a line-by-line owner-earnings calculation, so the direction of the corrected value remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Calculate FY2025 OE from the filed statements using the existing methodology, reconcile first-half 2026 operating results and noncash items, and rerun all scenarios with the corrected latest-actual anchor.

audit_findings.title: All $2.262 billion of cash may not be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.262bn, equal to $12.60 per diluted share and 42.6% of the $5.311bn base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar to equity value
audit_findings.evidence: We believe our current Cash and cash equivalents , along with future internally generated cash flow and funds available under our credit facilities, will provide sufficient resources to fund currently planned capital projects and our liquidity needs for the foreseeable future.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash balance is filed, but its status as entirely excess cash is not demonstrated. The filing identifies cash as funding operating liquidity, capital projects, dividends and repurchases. Because the full addition represents nearly half of base equity value, even a substantial operating-cash reserve could materially lower value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash to minimum operating liquidity, working-capital requirements, committed capital and turnaround spending, environmental and retirement obligations, financing proceeds and restricted amounts; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Cash turnaround spending may be missing from maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $413m FY2024 cash turnaround expenditures, equal to 190.3% of the $217m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if turnaround amortization is added back without deducting corresponding recurring turnaround and catalyst cash spending
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, for the year ended December 31, 2024, turnaround expenditures were $413 million compared to $556 million for the year ended December 31, 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The $413m cash expenditure is filed and large enough to eliminate the anchor if wholly omitted, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation already deducted actual or normalized turnaround spending. This is therefore a material unresolved calculation possibility, not a demonstrated omission.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2024 OE line by line, separately identifying PP&E maintenance capital, turnaround and catalyst cash spending, turnaround amortization and any normalization; rerun if cash turnaround economics were omitted or double counted.

audit_findings.title: Mandatory environmental spending may remain ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $137m gross disclosed program cost, equal to $0.76 per diluted share and 2.6% of $5.311bn base equity value; the unpaid unreflected portion is lower but unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unaccrued and unforecast cash obligation should reduce forecast OE or be deducted once in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Finally, HFS Navajo must implement injunctive relief and mitigation measures at an estimated cost of $137 million, including capital investments, at the Artesia refinery, certain of which measures have already been implemented as of the date of filing this Annual Report on Form 10-K and the remainder of which must be completed by various deadlines, ending in 2031.
audit_findings.explanation: The remaining unreflected amount is unresolved, but even the entire $137m disclosed program cost would reduce base value by only about 2.6% before recognizing that some measures were already implemented, $30m is included in 2026 capital guidance, and environmental liabilities are accrued. That scale is not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the remaining Navajo obligation at June 2026 against the $210m of filed current and noncurrent environmental liabilities and the $30m included in 2026 capital guidance; deduct only any unaccrued, unforecast remainder.

audit_findings.title: A noncash inventory reversal may be embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $43m pre-tax, equal to 19.8% of the $217m anchor; after-tax valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in OE, the noncash benefit raises the anchor and is propagated through forecast years and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2024, we recognized a lower of cost or market inventory valuation adjustment benefit of $43 million compared to a charge of $271 million for the year ended December 31, 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $43m FY2024 benefit is filed and economically nonrecurring, but the record does not show whether it was removed from calculated OE. Its size relative to the anchor and its multiplication through the DCF make the possible inclusion material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2024 LCM adjustment and associated tax effect through OE, confirm symmetric treatment of prior charges and subsequent reversals, and rerun the valuation if the benefit remains in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize an unusually low tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: 15.6% FY2024 effective rate versus 19.9% FY2025 and 23.3% for first-half 2026; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Growing reported after-tax OE can carry a temporary tax-rate benefit into forecast and terminal cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: The difference between the effective tax rate and the statutory rate for the year ended December 31, 2024 is principally due to the relationship between pre-tax earnings and benefits attributable to nontaxable permanent differences, offset by an increase in state income taxes and unrecognized tax benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: Later filed rates support the concern that FY2024's tax burden was unusually low, but effective tax rates contain discrete items and nontaxable renewable-fuel incentives that cannot be applied mechanically to every OE component. The record does not establish whether the model normalized cash taxes or how much of the rate difference is sustainable.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild cash taxes for FY2024 and FY2025 by separating recurring taxes, renewable-fuel incentives, state taxes and discrete items; rerun OE using the resulting sustainable tax burden.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $163.6m FY2022 residual, 24.9% of FY2022 filed D&A; $0 computed impact on the current $217m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense would understate historical OE and potentially the trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $163.6m (24.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The quantified residual relates to FY2022. Adding it back could only raise the historical trend, which is already $274m and therefore above the $217m latest-actual anchor selected by the MIN rule. It consequently has no effect on the current anchor or valuation, although unclassified FY2024 or FY2025 D&A could matter in a corrected rerun.
audit_findings.action: Classify residual D&A for FY2024 and FY2025 using filed asset and amortization disclosures; rerun only for components demonstrated to be eligible non-economic add-backs.
